commit.subject: feat(steme): add steme packages and policy-resolution core, unwired
commit.body:
Package the shipped rulepack as @steme-lab/rulepack-boundaries, create
@steme-lab/stackpack-steme composing it (rulepacks as real npm
dependencies), install the stackpack at the workspace root, and declare
the policy line in steme.workspace.json — all inert, nothing reads them
yet. Add the policy-resolution machinery behind a PackageResolverPort
(createRequire + realpath node adapter): workspace-manifest walk-up
discovery, minimal workspace parse, Zod stackpack parse, and policy →
ordered rulepack refs. Integration tests prove resolution against the real
pnpm symlink layout and against the hand-built temp-workspace layout the
E2E migration will use — retiring the riskiest unknown before the flip.

phases.title: Packages, policy resolution core, and the temp-workspace proof

commit.subject: feat(steme): load rules through the workspace policy; refuse STEME_RULEPACK
commit.body:
The audit preflight's rulepack step now resolves the workspace policy —
nearest steme.workspace.json above cwd, policy package via the resolver
port, stackpack expansion in declared order — with the hardcoded default
path deleted and a set STEME_RULEPACK refused with an actionable message
rather than honored or ignored. Multiple rulepacks evaluate as an ordered
union with per-rule skill provenance, per-pack validation, and
duplicate-rule-id rejection. All temp-rulepack fixtures migrate to
temporary workspaces exercising the real resolver; the non-override E2E
suites pass unmodified, pinning identical diagnostics and fingerprints
through the policy path.

phases.title: Policy becomes the sole rule source; the override is refused
